changes.before: If NDEBUG is defined, does this negative input become accepted?
changes.after: An assertion checks a programmer's assumption. Required input checks must still work when assertions are disabled.

before: assert from assert.h checks an expression unless NDEBUG was defined when the header was processed. Never put required input validation or necessary side effects only inside assert: a build may remove it.

This function rejects negative minutes with an ordinary if, independent of assertion mode. The assertion documents an internal condition after validation. The changed NDEBUG build must still reject the same bad input.
Expected output or behavior: 0. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Move an increment out of an assertion and explain why required work must not disappear in release builds. You may trace it without a C compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: An assertion checks that an assumption is true. If an enabled assert check fails, it stops the program. Defining NDEBUG before including assert.h disables these checks, so never put required work only inside assert.

Validation means checking whether input is allowed. This function uses an ordinary if to reject negative minutes. The later assertion checks an internal fact that should already be true after validation.
The input is -1. The if returns 0 before reaching the assertion, so main prints 0. The program handles this invalid input without depending on an assertion.
With NDEBUG defined, the assert expression is removed. The ordinary if still runs, so the same negative input is rejected.

before.question: If NDEBUG is defined, does this negative input become accepted?
choices: No: the ordinary if still returns zero.
Yes: NDEBUG removes all if statements.
The program must abort on every input.
before.explanation: Only the assertion macro is disabled; required validation remains normal C control flow.

after.question: If NDEBUG is defined, does the negative input become accepted?
choices: No; the ordinary if still returns 0.
Yes; NDEBUG removes all if statements.
The program must stop on every input.
after.explanation: Disabling assert does not remove ordinary validation. The if still rejects negative minutes.
